newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Southeast power rises ahead of cooler weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Southeast power rises ahead of cooler weather.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the U.S. Southeast edged higher Tuesday as a cooler blast of air moved toward the region and natural gas prices rebounded, market sources said.

Temperatures in the Southeast are expected to remain about 10 to 15 degrees F above normal through early Wednesday. Near- to slightly below-normal temperatures are forecast for the region Thursday and into the weekend as a cool front moves in from the Midwest.
Firm, peak power prices into Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) for Wednesday were mostly higher in the $16.00-17.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) range from Monday's trading at $14.75-16.00.
TVA's 1,065 MW Browns Ferry 2 nuclear power unit in Alabama remained at 29 percent of capacity this morning.
Firm, off-peak power prices into TVA were also talked higher at $14.00 per MWh.
At the Georgia/Florida border, firm, peak power prices in 16 hour blocks for Wednesday were also slightly stronger in the $19.00-21.00 per MWh range.
Firm, off-peak power for Wednesday at the Ga./Fla. border was assessed at $14.00 per MWh.
In Florida, firm, peak power prices on a 16-hour schedule for Wednesday were talked in the $18.75-20.50 range, while 24-hour power deals were reported done around $18.75.
Separately, Florida Power and Light Co's 666 MW Turkey Point 4 was operating at 60 percent output for cleaning and maintenance.
Returning to full power were Georgia Power's 741 MW Hatch 1, Virginia Power's 781 MW Surry 1 and Southern Co's 822 MW Farley 2 in Alabama.
Duke Power's 846 MW Oconee 2 nuclear unit in South Carolina, shut since last September after a steam pipe burst, was operating at 25 percent power early Tuesday.
Oconee unit 1 will likely restart later this week, the company said, while unit 3 is expected to resume power output this month.
Both units have a generating capacity of 846 MW each.
In congruence with the power market, natural gas prices along the Gulf Coast rose by about 10 cents today to the $2.53-2.60 per million British thermal units range.
